title: Building Apokerlypse with AI: testing the poker rules separately from the visuals
author: selcouth6
selftext:
I'm the creator of Apokerlypse, a free browser Texas Hold'em beta built with AI-assisted coding and AI-generated visual assets. It uses virtual chips only: no real money, account or download.



The most useful part of the workflow has been testing the game state separately from the presentation. The server controls the cards and chips; regression tests check split pots, hidden cards, reconnects and actions arriving after a turn has ended. The hosted backend is tested locally with an in-memory database.



A small example from today's local-server audit: a nickname like Élodie could turn into replacement characters if its UTF-8 bytes arrived in separate HTTP chunks. A network-level regression caught that even though ordinary room creation worked. Fixing it meant reassembling the bytes before decoding, not changing the interface.



Tests still don't tell me whether the table makes sense at a glance. You can try a few hands against labelled bots here: [https://apokerlypse.pages.dev](https://apokerlypse.pages.dev)



If you try it, is it immediately clear whose turn it is and how much you need to call? For other AI-assisted game developers, what manual checks have caught issues your automated tests missed?
